title: Cap. VIII: Adam–Christ opposition; major false for mediate view
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles now claims a twofold harvest from verse 19. Harvest one uses the opposition's force: the way we are made sinners in Adam matches the way we are made righteous in Christ; and we are made righteous in Christ by having his righteousness imputed; so we are made sinners in Adam by having his sin imputed. Placeus grants that the closing line need not wound readers who already hold mediate imputation — yet he still calls the opening line false. The difference the leading writers already marked (and Placeus already cited) is this: sinners by inhering sin carried into us and deserving death; not righteous by inhering righteousness deserving life.
pass_b_english: From this he thinks he can draw a double argument. First from the force of the opposition: we are constituted sinners in Adam by the same reason we are constituted righteous in Christ; but in Christ we are constituted righteous by the imputation of his righteousness; therefore in Adam we are constituted sinners by the imputation of his sin. Even though the conclusion does not harm those of us who acknowledge mediate imputation, the major premise is false. On the very point in dispute the greatest men marked a difference, as our earlier replies already showed. For we were constituted sinners by inhering sin propagated into us that deserves death; we were not constituted righteous by inhering righteousness that deserves life.
source_text: Hinc duplex argumentum se posse putat colligere: primum ex vi oppositionis. Eadem ratione constituimur peccatores in Adamo, qua justi constituimur in Christo. Atqui in Christo justi constituimur per justitiae ipsius imputationem. Ergo & peccatores in Adamo per peccati ipsius imputationem. Etsi nobis conclusio non nocet imputationem mediatam agnoscentibus, tamen major propositio falsa est. In eo enim ipso, de quo agitur, discrimen observatum est à viris maximis, uti patuit ex superioribus nostris responsionibus. Constituti enim sumus peccatores propagato in nos peccato inhaerente quod meretur mortem, non sumus constituti justi justitia inhaerente quae mereatur vitam.
